global_limits.repair_pass_rule: allowed once, only on failed_no_sources / failed_no_rows / zero relevant rows; before/after preserved

execution_protocol: run through the official CLI (PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m research_engine.cli run ...), deepest applicable mode
save full command, env facts, elapsed time in benchmarks/<ID>/notes.md and commands.jsonl
engine writes run dirs under runs/ (its native output path); audit analysis stays in audits/
inspect run_manifest, query_plan, collection_execution, evidence.jsonl, evidence_quality, claim_review, decision_brief, loop_contract, loop_record, research_report
compare planned vs executed vs returned sources; check timestamps, URLs, duplicates, conflicts, truncation, staleness, unsupported claims
any evidence gathered outside the engine is External Fallback: label it, record what engine capability gap forced it

benchmarks.title: Fast-moving market research: DRAM/HBM memory pricing as of 2026-07-16
benchmarks.user_question: What is the current state of DRAM/HBM pricing and supply tightness, with real-time prices and primary announcements?
benchmarks.decision_outcome: Investor-style brief: is supply tightness thesis still supported by CURRENT evidence?
benchmarks.command: run 'DRAM HBM memory contract price supply July 2026' --pack auto --depth deep --platform-scope all --web-search-pages --source-timeout-seconds 30
benchmarks.expected_artifacts: full 11-file bundle; finance rows with prices; seed pages fetched
benchmarks.repair_trigger: zero rows or all web seeds fail
benchmarks.success_rubric: 5=current prices + >=2 primary announcements inside window + stale seeds flagged; 3=prices but seed evidence stale and NOT flagged; 1=only quotes; 0=no rows
benchmarks.known_design_probe: memory_cycle pack seeds are dated 2026-03/06 — does the engine detect that seed evidence is older than the freshness window?

benchmarks.title: Deep technical research: vLLM vs SGLang inference engine architecture
benchmarks.user_question: Compare vLLM and SGLang: architecture, scheduling approach, current release lines, adoption.
benchmarks.decision_outcome: Engineering choice memo grounded in official docs/repos/papers.
benchmarks.command: run 'vLLM SGLang LLM inference engine architecture comparison' --pack auto --depth audit --platform-scope all --web-search-pages --source-timeout-seconds 30
benchmarks.min_source_diversity: 3 domains incl. github.com + at least one docs site
benchmarks.expected_artifacts: github_public_search rows; platform search page rows
benchmarks.repair_trigger: no github rows or zero relevant rows
benchmarks.success_rubric: 5=both projects' repos + versions + architectural facts extractable; 3=repos found but no versions/architecture text; 1=irrelevant repos; 0=no rows

benchmarks.title: Contested topic: DRAM oversupply vs shortage outlook
benchmarks.user_question: Is memory heading to oversupply or continued shortage into 2027? Both evidence chains required.
benchmarks.decision_outcome: Support and opposition chains with calibrated confidence.
benchmarks.command: run 'DRAM oversupply glut inventory correction versus shortage tight supply 2027 outlook' --pack auto --depth deep --web-search-pages --source-timeout-seconds 30
benchmarks.expected_artifacts: evidence_quality.conflict_flags populated (availability_pressure set); claim_review reflecting both directions
benchmarks.success_rubric: 5=conflict flag with both chains + confidence reflects conflict; 3=conflict flagged but synthesis ignores it; 1=one-sided evidence, no flag; 0=no rows
benchmarks.known_design_probe: does directional term co-occurrence produce a real support/oppose chain or just flag noise?

benchmarks.title: Niche topic, no pack/seed: JSON Canvas file format adoption
benchmarks.user_question: What is the JSON Canvas spec (from Obsidian), who has adopted it, current status?
benchmarks.decision_outcome: Adoption assessment for a niche open spec.
benchmarks.command_pass1: run 'JSON Canvas open file format spec adoption' --pack auto --depth deep --source-timeout-seconds 30
benchmarks.expected_artifacts: pass1 expected failed_no_sources (generic pack has zero sources) — that outcome is itself the autonomous-discovery measurement
benchmarks.success_rubric: 5=repair finds spec repo + adopters; 3=finds spec repo only; 1=irrelevant rows; 0=both passes empty

benchmarks.title: GitHub ecosystem survey: open-source deep research agents
benchmarks.user_question: What are the leading open-source deep-research agent frameworks; maintenance, license, releases?
benchmarks.decision_outcome: Discovery seed list for Phase 3 with maintenance/license signals.
benchmarks.command: run 'open source deep research agent framework' --pack auto --depth audit --platform-scope all --source-timeout-seconds 30
benchmarks.expected_artifacts: github_public_search rows with stars/forks/language; NO license/release/issue fields (known schema gap to verify)
benchmarks.success_rubric: 5=relevant repos + license + releases + maintenance; 3=relevant repos, metrics only; 1=irrelevant repos (query normalization strips 'open source'/'repo' — probe); 0=no rows

benchmarks.title: Adversarial sources: JS-heavy, blocked, 404, malformed, PDF
benchmarks.user_question: Fetch a seed set designed to fail: x.com search (bot-gated), a JS-only SPA, a 404, an invalid TLD, a PDF URL.
benchmarks.decision_outcome: Failure transparency: are failures visible, honest, and non-blocking?
benchmarks.method: custom audit-only pack via --pack-dir audits/.../fixtures/packs (does not touch repo packs/)
benchmarks.command: run 'adversarial fetch degradation audit' --pack b6_adversarial --pack-dir <audit>/fixtures/packs --depth deep --source-timeout-seconds 30
benchmarks.expected_artifacts: collection_execution with per-source failures; access_blocked flags; PDF garbage-text probe
benchmarks.success_rubric: 5=every failure individually visible w/ reason + run status honest; 3=failures visible but status misleading (e.g. 'complete' with 90% blocked); 1=silent drops; 0=crash

benchmarks.title: Longitudinal rerun: cache, freshness, diff
benchmarks.user_question: Re-run B1's topic twice with --cache-dir: does the second run reuse cache, detect changes, or diff?
benchmarks.command: 2x run 'DRAM HBM memory contract price supply July 2026' --pack auto --depth quick --cache-dir <audit>/fixtures/cache --source-timeout-seconds 30
benchmarks.expected_artifacts: run2 collection_execution.status_counts.cache_hit > 0; no diff artifact exists (expected capability gap)
benchmarks.success_rubric: 5=cache hits + diff/freshness policy; 3=cache hits, no diff (predicted); 1=no cache hits despite flag; 0=error
benchmarks.known_design_probe: cache key includes run_date — same-day rerun should hit, cross-day never; no TTL

benchmarks.title: Mixed formats: authorized JSONL + PDF + HTML table
benchmarks.user_question: Combine tests/fixtures/stripe_false_positive_evidence.jsonl (pre-existing, authorized) with a public PDF and a table-heavy HTML page.
benchmarks.decision_outcome: Format handling: JSONL import fidelity, PDF text extraction, table structure preservation.
benchmarks.command: run 'mixed format evidence handling audit' --pack b8_mixed --pack-dir <audit>/fixtures/packs --external-evidence tests/fixtures/stripe_false_positive_evidence.jsonl --depth deep --source-timeout-seconds 30
benchmarks.expected_artifacts: external_jsonl rows normalized; PDF row expected garbage/empty (probe); table flattened to linear text (probe)
benchmarks.success_rubric: 5=all formats structured; 3=JSONL ok, PDF/table degraded but flagged; 1=degraded silently; 0=import fails
